newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lesotho opposition walks out of parliament.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho opposition walks out of parliament.

text.p: Lesotho's newly created opposition walked out of parliament on Wednesday in protest against Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle's formation of a new governing party at the weekend, the opposition chairman said.

Mokhehle, the ageing and ailing prime minister, formed the Lesotho Congress for Democracy Party with a faction of the ruling Basotholand Congress Party, taking with him a majority of the 65 members of parliament to form a new party in power.
About 20 BCP members have refused to recognise the new party and have threatened to approach southern African countries for assistance, said party chairman Ntsuknyane Mphanya.
"We regard what Mokhehle did as a bloodless coup. We cannot take part in a government of such a nature because we consider the BCP to be the legitimate government," he told Reuters.
The party has lodged a complaint with the monarch of the tiny landlocked kingdom, King Letsie III, and was waiting for a reply before taking any action, Mphanya said.
"We will not approach the South African Development Community (SADC) for help yet. At present we will deal with this struggle by ourselves," he said.
Lesotho, with two million citizens, is one of the smallest of SADC's 12 members and is heavily reliant on South Africa, which encircles it, for imports and work.
It has no major exports apart from abundant water which it sells to South Africa's industries.
The BCP members would attend parliamentary prayers on Thursday, but not stay longer than that, Mphanya said.
"We are not prepared to take any discussion on this matter."
